To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural information collected by crystallographers may possess a great potential for the discovery of new facts and theories in chemistry, provided systematic methods for database analysis and crystallographic interpretation are made available.

(1) the structural information collected by diffraction studies of crystals of organic molecules is a valuable resource that can be used as a basis of new scientific discoveries; (2) SCMs are the methods of choice for the systematic analysis and the interpretation of this resource; (3) SCMs are based upon the systematic search for, and recognition of, correlations among structural parameters of the same molecular fragments found in many different structures; (4) SCMs can be used to discover new chemical facts or
the structure correlation methods (or SCMs) are powerful heuristic tools that allow the discovery of new structural information, new chemical facts or new chemical theories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of SCMs for crystal structure interpretation.
the development and application of structure correlation methods (structural informatics) in chemical crystallography.
the development and use of structure correlation methods (structural informatics) in the study of molecular crystals and other crystalline materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SCMs are a powerful tool for the analysis of structural databases and for the interpretation of the structural information contained in them, and that they can be used to guide the formulation of new theories in crystal structure chemistry and in the chemistry of molecular materials in general, including the chemistry of organic materials, the chemistry of molecular magnets, molecular electronics and molecular materials science.
